subject: ACMECloud: Clarify usage identity handoff + webhook sample for AWS Marketplace
messages:
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acmecloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements <procurements@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACMECloud: Clarify usage identity handoff + webhook sample for AWS Marketplace

Hi Sergio / Neha,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. Our procurement and marketplace engineering teams need a clearer picture of how Redwood expects identity and entitlement to flow between AWS Marketplace, our SaaS account model, and your fulfillment callbacks. Two short asks to unblock internal approval: 

1) A one-page mapping of which IDs we must send from the Marketplace metering/fulfillment payload (e.g., Marketplace Entitlement ID, Customer AWS Account ID, customer_email, org_id) to ensure seats/consumption align to our billing system.
2) A sample webhook payload and a minimal retry/backoff expectation (how Redwood will surface duplicate events or missed deliveries).

We have a sandbox environment available but need your checklist for what credentials and test SKUs you expect. If you can send the mapping and a sample webhook today, I'll loop in our infra lead to provision access.

Regards,

--
Claire Johnson
Head of Procurement, AcmeCloud Analytics
claire.johnson@acmecloud.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: none
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACMECloud: Clarify usage identity handoff + webhook sample for AWS Marketplace

Claire — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Mapping: we map the Marketplace entitlement to your internal account via the marketplace_entitlement_id and a customer-provided external_account_id (we can accept AWS account ID or your internal org_id). We prefer a deterministic field mapping rather than email.
- Webhook: we will POST usage/fulfillment events to a configured HTTPS endpoint. We include an idempotency key and event_timestamp. Our SDK expects a 2xx to mark delivered; we retry with exponential backoff for 5 attempts.

What we need from you to spin up the sandbox:
- Sandbox webhook endpoint (URL) + TLS cert thumbprint (or let us host a temporary endpoint).
- Example mapping table: which of your internal fields correspond to AWS account ids or org ids.
- One or two SKU/test-entitlement IDs to exercise usage calls.

I attached a tiny sample payload (metering_webhook_sample.json) and a short field mapping suggestion inlined below. We can jump on a 30–60m technical call — propose Wed 2027-06-02 09:00 PT or Thu 2027-06-03 11:00 PT.

Field mapping suggestion (minimal):
- marketplace_entitlement_id -> acme_entitlement_id
- external_account_id -> acme_org_id or aws_account_id
- usage_metric -> compute_units|api_calls
- units_consumed -> integer (per-minute granularity)

Attachment: metering_webhook_sample.json (application/json)

Let me know which slot works and I'll get our infra/engineer on the invite.

Thanks,

--
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acmecloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements <procurements@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACMECloud: Clarify usage identity handoff + webhook sample for AWS Marketplace

Sergio — appreciate the quick turnaround. Answers below and attaching our entitlement spec.

1) Mapping: we will provide acme_org_id (our canonical org id) and we can also include customer_aws_account_id for customers who subscribe via AWS. We prefer org-level billing (one org_id per paying tenant). Please treat customer_email as optional for lookups.

2) Webhook endpoint: we've provisioned a sandbox listener at https://sandbox.acmecloud.com/marketplace/webhook and will add Redwood's IP / cert. Our network team says they will accept mutual TLS if you prefer.

3) Reliability: we'll expect idempotency behavior for duplicate events. If you keep an event_id + idempotency_key, we can dedupe on our side. For missed deliveries, we'll provide a temporary webhook replay UI but want to avoid long-term replay as our billing system expects near-real-time events.

Attached: ACME_SaaS_Entitlement_Spec.pdf (describes acme_org_id, internal sku mapping and contract granularity) and metering_webhook_sample.json. Below is an excerpt of the payload we'll send for fulfillment / usage events (sanitized):

{
  "event_id": "evt-20270601-0001",
  "marketplace_entitlement_id": "mpx-ent-9982",
  "external_account_id": "acme-org-214",
  "customer_aws_account_id": "123456789012",
  "usage_metric": "compute_units",
  "units_consumed": 120,
  "event_timestamp": "2027-06-01T15:18:00Z"
}

We'll upload the PDF and sample JSON to the shared Drive after this thread; attaching small copies here as well.

Thanks — Claire

Attachment: ACME_SaaS_Entitlement_Spec.pdf (application/pdf - 1.2MB), metering_webhook_sample.json (application/json - 2KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACMECloud: Clarify usage identity handoff + webhook sample for AWS Marketplace

Claire — thanks for the attachments and the sandbox URL. Quick internal recap and proposed runbook so procurement and infra have clear next steps: 

1) Credentialing / sandbox prep (owner: Acme infra)
- Redwood needs (a) an HTTPS endpoint with valid cert or allowlist of our outbound IPs and (b) test SKUs + sample entitlements.

2) Field mapping (owner: Redwood / confirm with Acme)
- marketplace_entitlement_id -> acme_entitlement_id (primary match)
- external_account_id -> acme_org_id (canonical payer)
- customer_aws_account_id -> optional: stored for traceability
- usage_metric -> canonical metric name (we propose compute_units)

3) Delivery semantics (owner: Redwood)
- Delivery: Redwood will POST events, include event_id and idempotency_key, expect 2xx.
- Retries: exponential backoff up to 5 attempts, then mark for manual retry and email the Acme webhook-ops mailbox.

4) Canaries and cutover (owner: joint)
- Start with a canary group (5 customers) for 7 days, verify reconciliation vs Acme ledger daily.
- If canary passes, run gradual ramp (25% / 50% / 100%).

Action items:
- Claire to confirm the 30–60m technical slot (we prefer Wed 2027-06-09 09:00 PT).
- Acme to provide test SKUs and enable Redwood IP/cert allowlist.
- Redwood infra (Marcus) will prepare a short runbook and small replay helper for missed events.

I'll prepare the runbook and share a Drive link. If you want, we can also provide a short Postman collection for your QA team.

Best,

--
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
